syllabus: First assessment 2021; course examinations through 2028, excluding the first-assessment-2029 revision
checkedAgainst: Official guide syllabus tables and assessment outlines; official specimen examiner instructions and representative question/markscheme pages. Original practice content is independently authored; no specimen question text is reused.

boundaries: Radian trig and the ambiguous sine case are included; compound-angle identities and inverse-trig function analysis are additional HL.
Product, quotient and chain rules belong to AA SL5.6.
Graph transformations f(ax+b) are outside the SL transformation requirement; factor/remainder theorems and polynomial-root relations are additional HL.
First-principles differentiation, analytical limits, induction, complex numbers, vectors, probability densities and hypothesis tests are outside this SL question set.
Degree-based circles, perpendicular bisectors and Voronoi diagrams; radians are not required.
Finance includes amortization and annuities with technology.
Spearman rank correlation, chi-square tests and pooled unpaired two-sample t-tests are SL; inference follows the guide restrictions.
Chi-square exam examples use expected frequencies greater than 5 and degrees of freedom greater than one; goodness-of-fit degrees of freedom equal categories minus one.

Analytic calculus uses integer powers; chain/product/quotient rules and transcendental derivatives belong to additional HL. Optimisation and trapezoids are SL; SL examination questions on kinematics are excluded.

Function composition notation, general inverse derivation with domain restriction and graph transformations belong to AI additional HL; SL includes the informal inverse concept and graphical interpretation.
SL topics remain part of the HL course; level marks the demand of the item, not its containing course.

Additional HL covers generalized binomial/counting, partial fractions, complex numbers, proof, systems; further functions, vectors and planes; Bayes and random-variable moments; advanced calculus, differential equations and Maclaurin series.
No identical-object permutations or circular arrangements are required. Partial fractions use at most two distinct linear factors with proper numerator.
First-principles derivative proofs use polynomials. Questions asking students to test continuity/differentiability are explicitly excluded from examinations.
For integration substitutions outside the reverse-chain form, supply the substitution.

marking.A1: One distinct accuracy/result award, dependent on the associated method when present.
marking.R1: One distinct justified reasoning or interpretation award.
marking.givenAnswer: A supplied result earns no accuracy mark merely by being copied.
marking.followThrough: Credit correct subsequent work after an earlier error when the changed value does not trivialize or invalidate the demand; show the required later method.
marking.alternatives: Credit mathematically equivalent forms and valid alternative methods within the stated domain and precision.
marking.precision: Retain unrounded working; follow the stated precision. Unless stated otherwise, non-exact numerical answers are given to three significant figures.
